messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER: Incident triggered INC-20260315 - routing errors spike across prod. Link: https://pd.redwood.example/INC-20260315 :rotating_light: Started 3412345678

alex_k: investigating. seeing a big fanout of routing requests to multiple model variants. paging @mia.ng for oncall.

mia.ng: on it, grabbing logs now. any customer-facing impact reported?

alex_k: yes - a couple customers saw 503s and some responses returned from legacy variant ids (e.g. gpt-x-legacy) instead of pinned variants. audit shows policy broadcast to many variants. here's an audit line from the routing service: ```[3412345665] route_request user=acct-42 request_id=req-9a8b variant_targets=[gpt-x, gpt-x-legacy, gpt-y, gpt-z] policy=automatic_fallback```

jordan: this aligns with the config-schema v2 rollout we pushed earlier (3412345600). we deprecated the field `preferred_variant` and the control plane now treats missing preferred_variant as an empty array, which our fallback logic interprets as "no preference -> broadcast to all compatible variants". that broadcast caused cross-region fanout and some region failback loops.

pat: metrics show region bouncing between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 for the same requests. pods spun up in eu-west then us-east because of fallback loops, GPU pools saturated. CPU/GPU % utilization -> ```gpu_util: 92%, pod_spinups: +420/min```

alex_k: proposed mitigations: 1) disable automatic fallback globally 2) pin routing policy for affected accounts 3) rollback config-schema rollout in config-service 4) temp rate-limit variant targets to N<=3 per request. who can flip the fallback toggle?

mia.ng: I can flip it. doing toggle now.

oncall-bot: ACTION: fallback_toggle false (changed by mia.ng) at 3412345720

mia.ng: fallback disabled. monitoring for immediate effects.

pat: running pin script to update affected accounts: ```curl -X POST https://config.redwood.example/api/v1/routing/pin -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"account_id":"acct-42","routing":{"variant":"gpt-x-stable"}}'``` will iterate through the 8 highest-impact accounts.

alex_k: rolling back config-service to release/20260314 now (k8s rollout restart). command: ```kubectl -n control-plane rollout undo deploy/config-service --to-revision=234```

jordan: after disabling fallback and pinning, errors dropped back to baseline and pod spinups normalized. looks like immediate mitigation worked. still collecting logs for full scope.

customer-success-bot: Notified CSMs for top affected customers (acct-42, acct-87, acct-19). templates: "We're investigating increased errors/latency and will follow up within 1 hour."

luis: quick impact summary for initial notification: 8 customers affected, window ~3412345600 - 3412345890, peak latency ~2.8x, some 503s and unexpected variant IDs in audit logs. no evidence of data exfiltration.

mia.ng: handing off to @luis for follow-up and postmortem. luis, you're on for the night.

luis: ack, taking over. will keep watch on metrics (routes/sec, variant_targets distribution) and gather trace IDs for escalation. starting log bundle collection.

alex_k: root cause notes for postmortem draft: schema change removed `preferred_variant` without a compatibility shim; runtime interpreted missing field as empty list -> policy broadcast. missing safety checks in control plane + no CI gating for deprecated field removals.

jordan: short-term remediation items: - add safe-default handling in routing runtime (treat missing preferred_variant as "no-change" rather than empty) - add CI test to block schema rollouts that remove fields without a compatibility migration - add alert for >5 variant targets per request and sudden variance in target count - implement runtime rate-limiter for variant fanout (N<=3)

mia.ng: implemented immediate firebreak: rate limit routing control plane to max 3 variant targets per request in the circuit-breaker config.

jordan: creating PD follow-up ticket INC-2345, severity set to SEV2. postmortem owner assigned to @alex_k.

oncall-bot: Incident acknowledged and assigned to luis at 3412345845. Next update in 30m.

alex_k: thanks all. we'll publish a postmortem with timeline, impact, root cause, and action items once logs and traces are consolidated. tagging @eng-runtime, @eng-ml, @product. closing this thread after postmortem link is shared. :white_check_mark:
